newsitem.title: HAITI: CIA "memo" reveals assassins of Haitian official.
newsitem.headline: CIA "memo" reveals assassins of Haitian official.

text.p: A self-described Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) informant planned the 1993 murder of Haiti's reformist justice minister, according to a purported CIA document released by a civil rights group on Friday.

The document, dated Oct. 28, 1993, says the Oct. 14, 1993, assassination of Justice Minister Guy Malary was planned by Emmanuel "Toto" Constant and other military officers including former Col. Philippe Biamby.
Constant, leader of a paramilitary group in Haiti under a 1991-94 military government, has repeatedly said he was paid $500 per month as a CIA informant.

The alleged CIA document was obtained by the Centre for Constitutional Rights in New York and made available to journalists on Friday. The U.S. Embassy declined to comment or to confirm if Constant was on the agency's payroll.
Biamby was the right-hand man of Lt. Gen. Raoul Cedras, who led the military coup that ousted then-President Jean-Bertrand Aristide in September 1991.

"In early to mid-October Biamby and his associates coordinated the murder of Justice Minister Guy Malary ... with members of the Revolutionary Front for Haitian Advancement and Progress (FRAPH)," according to the document.
Malary and two bodyguards were gunned down in his car as he left his office in the capital at the height of the military repression.
He had presented a plan to demilitarize the police days earlier and was trying to reform the justice system.
"FRAPH members Jodel Chamblain, Emmanuel Constant and Gabriel Douzablee met with an unidentified military officer on the morning of 14 October to discuss plans to kill Malary," the memo said.
Constant says the CIA continued to pay him in the months after the murder.
"The document states authoritatively that Constant and Biamby planned the assassination," CCR human rights attorney Michael Ratner said by telephone from New York.
"That they continued to pay him, and may have helped him leave the country, certainly seems reprehensible to me."
"They knew within days after the killing, and this is one of the more astounding things," said Ratner. "It is possible the CIA knew of the assassination contemporaneously."
The memo's release could increase tensions between the United States and the Haitian government, which wants Constant returned from New York to face justice.

Constant travelled to New York under a valid visa. He was eventually arrested by U.S. authorities but was recently released in a secret deal in which he was banned from political activity or discussing his ties to the CIA.
The U.S. government has claimed his return to Haiti would have a destabilising effect on the impoverished nation.
Biamby left Haiti after the military regime collapsed for Panama with Cedras on a U.S. military plane three years ago.

The Haitian Information Bureau said this week Biamby and a few dozen relatives were also flown out of the country and given access to frozen bank accounts totalling more than $79 million. They were also leased three homes by the U.S. government, it said.
Two alleged gunmen in the Malary assassination were tried in July but acquitted due to lack of evidence.
